locator.text: Equation (5.13), p. 50, in the statement of Lemma 5.2

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The weight, the edge distance and the domain match the paper exactly: `activeZeta c a b w = weight c a b (log X)` is the two-edge flat weight ζ(X); `activeDelta a b w = min 1 (min (log X - a) (b - log X))`, which with a = log X_a and b = log X_b is literally δ(X) = min{1, log(X/X_a), log(X_b/X)}; and `activeWindow a b = Ioo (exp a) (exp b) ×ˢ Icc (-1) 1` is {X_a < X < X_b, |η| ≤ 1}. `PolynomialEdgeJets` is then the paper's bound C ζ δ^{-N}, with two encoding choices in the Lean's favour: it bounds the whole derivative tensor ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m f w‖ at each order m (its docstring says 'including mixed derivatives') rather than each ∂^I separately, so one constant serves all multi-indices of a given order; and the constants C, N are existentially quantified per order m, matching 'C_{n,I}, N_{n,I} may depend on the order and derivative'. What differs is the range of n. The Lean states this bound for the stress only at order n = 1 (`firstStress_edgeJets` on the whole active annulus, `modulated_first_edgeJets` on the outer collar for the concrete modulated coefficients). For n ≥ 2 no per-order weighted jet bound was found; the repository reaches the same place by another route: `HigherInteriorSupport` (the n ≥ 2 stresses are supported in a compact sub-annulus, see `modulated_higherInteriorSupport`) gives `higherStressQuotient_smooth_of_support`, i.e. 𝒯_n/ζ is globally C^∞ for n ≥ 2, and that smoothness — not a ζδ^{-N} jet bound per order — is what is fed into `normalizedTensor_weighted_bound`, together with `activeZeta_edgeJets` for the weight itself and `compact_weighted_jet_bound` on compacta, to produce the all-order conclusion `ConstructedSlowBase.WeightedStressBound`, which carries the paper's ζ(X)δ(X)^{-N} shape for the assembled cut tensor. So the formula as the paper writes it, with n ≥ 2, is not a Lean statement; what is stated instead is strictly the factorization 𝒯_n = ζ · (smooth) plus compact support, from which (5.13) for n ≥ 2 follows by Leibniz on ζ · (𝒯_n/ζ) with `activeZeta_edgeJets` and boundedness of the quotient's derivatives on the compact closure of the window. I did not carry that derivation out in Lean, and I did not verify the paper's closing remark that one may take N_{n,I} = 0 for n ≥ 2 against anything stated in the repository.
